topic_title: Chapter 4 - Lesson 4-4 - The Iterative Improvement Process for Websites

questions.question: PDCA repeats the sequence Plan, Do, Check, Act.
Design thinking solves problems mainly from the developer's perspective.
A/B testing should change only one element at a time.
PDCA is complete after one execution of the four steps.
What improvement method repeats Plan, Do, Check, and Act?
What method prepares two patterns and compares their results using real user data?
Match each design-thinking description with the correct step: A Empathize, B Define, C Ideate, D Prototype, E Test.

items.text: Understand the user's challenges and needs.
Clarify the problem to be solved.
Let users try the design and collect feedback.

questions.question: Which activity corresponds to the 'Check' step in PDCA?
options: Measure the bounce rate after the change.
Decide what improvement to make next.

questions.question: Which is NOT appropriate when performing A/B testing?
options: Change multiple elements at the same time.
Show the patterns to actual users.

questions.question: Explain why a website team improves through repeated PDCA cycles instead of trying to build a perfect website in one attempt.
questions.model_answer: The first version is a best guess. The team measures actual results, checks whether the goal was achieved, and uses the evidence to decide the next improvement. Repeating the cycle gradually improves the website.

questions.question: A website team wants to compare two purchase-button designs. Explain how they could use A/B testing correctly.
questions.model_answer: Prepare option A and option B, show them to actual users, and compare real data such as clicks. Only one element should be changed at a time, and sufficient data should be collected before deciding which option is more effective.
